rubrics.justification: The response incorrectly states no Gardner score was available and does not analyze the provided 3AA morphology; it substitutes an assumed average-quality blastocyst, omitting the actual expansion, ICM, and TE features.

It integrates most relevant factors well, including age, ovarian reserve markers, prior cycle, BMI, sperm quality, and day-5 blastocyst status, though it misses the prognostic significance of the actual 3AA grade.

The reasoning is generally structured and internally understandable, but it is weakened by the false premise that morphology data were unavailable and by probability estimates based on an assumed average embryo rather than the known 3AA embryo.

Much of the discussion is broadly evidence-based, but recommending ERA after a single failed cycle and suggesting PGT-A in a 28-year-old without stronger indication are not strongly guideline-supported; failure to use the provided Gardner grade also detracts.

The recommendations are practical and clinically usable, covering endometrial assessment, luteal support, diagnostic clarification, and future planning, though some suggestions are somewhat overreaching for this specific case.
